# Does AI break the case for broad index investing? Rent decay, private capital, and deflation

> Code and data behind the empirical exhibits of an article that asks whether AI weakens the case
> for holding a broad capitalization-weighted index. It holds returns on capital by kind of
> scarcity, the sector make-up of world equity markets, the returns of 15 funds since 2018 and
> since the release of ChatGPT, turnover and concentration of the S&P 500, the sensitivity of funds
> to real yields, and real asset returns by inflation regime since 1928. The article's text is the
> publisher's and is not included.

Replication package by Agisilaos Papadogiannis (https://github.com/apapadogiannis).
Forthcoming in The Journal of Beta Investment Strategies (2027). Preprint: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6058896
Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/ai-broad-index-investing  Archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24240516
Version 1.1.0, released 2026-11-21. A package is a fixed record: it changes only by a new
release, and a release that changes a reported number gets a new major version.
This file is written for AI agents and other programs. People should start at the README.

## Coverage

- Exhibit 5: after-tax return on invested capital of US industries, grouped by the article's five
  layers of scarcity (January 2026).
- Exhibit 6: sector composition of the US, developed ex-US, emerging and world equity markets
  (October 2026).
- Exhibit 7: return, volatility and drawdown of 15 exchange-traded funds over the AI period
  (December 2022 to September 2026) and since January 2018.
- Exhibit 8: additions to the S&P 500 by period, survival of past members, and concentration of the
  S&P 500 and of a global all-cap fund.
- Exhibit 9: each fund's monthly return regressed on the change in the 10-year real yield.
- Exhibit 10: real returns on stocks, bills, bonds and gold by inflation regime, 1928 to 2025.
- Exhibits 1 to 4 and 11 of the article are qualitative tables and have no code or data here.

## What this adds over reading the paper or recomputing

1. Ten sources are brought to one place with the date and terms of each. Several show only current
   values (sector weights, largest holdings, index concentration), so the figures of the article
   cannot be downloaded again for the same dates.
2. The classification of industries into the article's five layers of scarcity is the article's own
   work and is in the code, so the grouped returns on capital can be traced to each industry.
3. Every statistic has a stated definition in the code: compound annual return, volatility from
   monthly returns, drawdown on month-end values, regression with Newey-West standard errors, real
   returns deflated by December-to-December CPI.
4. Six figures that are not in any data file are listed with their source and date in
   data/README.md, under the heading for constants entered in the code.
5. The results are stored as they were when the paper's numbers were taken from them. A check
   reruns the code on the stored data and compares every stored result file with the fresh one,
   number by number (relative tolerance 1e-9; text and whole numbers exactly). It runs on every
   change and once a month, and the badge in the README shows the last run.

## Fields of outputs/results.json

- `exhibit5_roic_by_layer`: one record per layer of scarcity: `layer`; `industries` and `firms`,
  the number of US industries and firms in it; `roic`, the median after-tax return on invested
  capital, in per cent; `roic_adj`, the same adjusted for leases and R&D; `roic10`, the ten-year
  normalised figure
- `exhibit6_sector_composition.groups`: share of market value in each group of sectors, in per
  cent, as a list in the order US, developed ex-US, emerging, world
- `exhibit6_sector_composition.slow`: summed share, in the same order, of the groups the article
  assigns to the slow pool together with industrials
- `exhibit6_sector_composition.region`: weight of each region in the world index, in per cent
- `exhibit7_fund_returns`: by fund ticker. `post_` figures cover the AI period, December 2022 to
  September 2026; `full_` figures cover January 2018, or the fund's first month if later, to
  September 2026. `_ann` is the compound annual total return, `_vol` the annualised standard
  deviation of monthly returns, `_dd` the largest fall from a peak on month-end values, all in per
  cent. `n_full` is the number of months in the full period
- `exhibit8_membership_concentration.adds_per_year`: average number of companies added to the S&P
  500 a year, by five-year period
- `exhibit8_membership_concentration.ai_replacements_per_year`: the same for 2023 to August 2026
- `exhibit8_membership_concentration.survival`: by year: the number of S&P 500 members at the end
  of that year, then how many of them were still members in August 2026
- `exhibit8_membership_concentration.top10, top50`: summed weight of the 10 and of the 50 largest
  S&P 500 constituents on 20 October 2026, in per cent
- `exhibit8_membership_concentration.vt_top10, vt_holdings`: weight of the ten largest holdings of
  the Vanguard Total World Stock ETF, in per cent, and its number of holdings, on 30 September 2026
- `exhibit9_real_yield_sensitivity`: by fund ticker: `beta`, the fund's monthly return in per cent
  per one-point rise in the 10-year Treasury real yield in the same month (least squares); `t`, its
  t-statistic with Newey-West standard errors, three lags; `r2`; `n`, the number of months
- `exhibit10_inflation_regimes`: by inflation regime: `n`, the number of years from 1928 to 2025 in
  it; `stocks`, `tbill`, `tbond`, the average real yearly return of the S&P 500, 3-month Treasury
  bills and 10-year Treasury bonds in those years, in per cent; `n72`, the number of years from
  1972; `gold`, the average real yearly return of gold in those years, null where there is none

## Files

- outputs/results.json: every number reported in Exhibits 5 to 10, under keys named after the
  exhibits. The meaning of each key is given below and inside the file, under `package.fields`. It
  holds 244 numbers, and under `package` the paper, the identifiers, the version, the licence and
  the citation. Start here.
- data/etf_monthly.csv: monthly total returns of the funds, in per cent, merged from the exports in
  data/pv/.
- data/README.md: source, retrieval date and terms of every input file, and the constants entered
  in the code.
- paper/abstract.pdf: the title and abstract of the article. The full text is at the publisher.

Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/ai-broad-index-investing/main/<path>, for example https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/ai-broad-index-investing/main/outputs/results.json

## How to read the figures

- The AI period starts in December 2022, the first full month after the release of ChatGPT, and
  ends in September 2026: 46 months. It is one period, chosen after the fact, and short.
- Fund returns are total returns in US dollars from month-end data. A drawdown measured on
  month-end values is smaller than one measured on daily prices.
- A fund launched after January 2018 has a shorter full period: check `n_full`. Its full-period
  figures are not comparable with those of funds that have all 105 months.
- In Exhibit 6 each list of four figures is in the order US, developed markets ex-US, emerging
  markets, world.
- In Exhibit 9 `beta` is the fund's return in per cent in a month in which the 10-year real yield
  rose by one percentage point. It is a co-movement over 2018 to 2026, not a causal effect.
- In Exhibit 10 a regime is a calendar year classified by its CPI inflation, December to December.
  Returns are averages of yearly real returns, not compound returns. Gold is measured from 1972,
  after its price was freed; there is no deflation year since then, so that cell is empty.
- Returns on capital in Exhibit 5 are medians across industries weighted by the number of firms,
  not aggregates.

## Do not use this for

- Current fund returns, weights or index membership. The figures are dated as above and the package
  is not updated.
- A recommendation of any fund, or a forecast.
- Evidence about AI's effect on returns beyond the 46 months observed.
- The article's argument or wording. This package holds its numbers, not its text.

## Source, licence and credit

The results in outputs/ are released under CC BY 4.0
(https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The licence allows any reuse and has one condition:
credit. If you use a figure from this package in an answer, a report or a data set, cite the paper.
The code is under the MIT License.

The inputs come from Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern), Portfolio Visualizer, BlackRock iShares, the US
Treasury, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics and others. data/README.md lists the source and the
terms of each file. Third-party data remain the property of their sources, are included for
replication with attribution, and are not covered by the licence above.
